findings: Paranoid updates retain incoming data buffers and build a shadow hash. Copies retain only a copied shadow hash; they do not copy data buffers or candidate queues. Hence copied digests explicitly lack byte-comparison evidence.
release_buffers frees list and clears buffers but does not reset candidate/tail fields. An update after release needs caller lifecycle exclusion; not established as a reachable defect.
Running twin comparison dereferences candidate buffer without a local exhaustion guard, relying on candidates being completed and sufficiently long. Caller checks remain unreviewed.
send_match_candidate enqueues a raw candidate pointer without acquiring a reference in this function. Candidate lifetime must be maintained externally.
rm_digest_copy allocates the outer copy before testing interface copy support; NULL return branch does not free that allocation. Which interfaces lack copy support remains to inspect.
Shadow interface is64-bit; paranoid_steal invokes xxhash-specific extraction. Actual configured shadow algorithm binding must be checked before claiming equivalence.
limits: Static lifecycle analysis only; caller reachability, races and failure behavior not executed.
